text:
maya: Heads-up — after the continuous-batcher timer tweak rolled to canary this morning, we're seeing tail latency spikes and a throughput drop on a subset of hosts. P95 went from ~420ms to ~1.2s on the canary fleet, throughput down ~18%.

leo: Ugh. Which tweak exactly? the microbatch timer skew compensation? :thinking:

maya: yep — the change made timers jitter less aggressive so small requests should coalesce more, but looks like in practice some workers form a bunch of small microbatches that trigger kernel fallback. logs attached below.

sam: can you paste the profiler traces / kernel switch lines?

maya: paste from the runtime logs: 
```
[2026-02-28T03:12:04Z] deploy-bot: canary rollout id=canary-20260228-0312
[runtime] p95_latency_ms=1200 p50=110 p99=1800 throughput_rps=-18% vs baseline
[kernel] kernel_switch: chosen=fast_kernel reason=load_shape mismatch fallback=slow_kernel count=1273
[kv] kv_prefetch: miss_rate=0.38 evictions_per_sec=240 prefetch_wait_ms_p50=42 p95=220
[batcher] microbatch_timer_skew_applied=true token_budget_target=64
```

maya: and a sampling from pprof (aggregated):
```
CPU: 1min sample
15% runtime/kv_prefetch_wait
12% runtime/kernel_copy_slowpath
10% scheduler/wake_latency
8% memory/kv_gc
```

olivia: my hypothesis: the timer tweak reduced one kind of jitter but introduced a bias where some queues start draining at slightly offset phases -> more small microbatches hit the kernel path that expects larger batch shapes -> kernel falls back to slow kernels and KV prefetch can't warm fast enough. So two amplifying effects: (1) batch size distribution shifted left, (2) prefetch evictions because KV cache TTL/size tuned for previous pattern.

rina: tracing corroborates that — the trace heatmap shows flow oscillation: host-level backlog oscillates between 0 and small spikes every 30-80ms window. That pattern matches the new timer alignment.

infra-bot: linked traces: https://redwood.internal/traces/trace/fe2b9a (canary hosts: canary-group-7)

leo: nice. Can we reproduce locally with the workload replay? If batch size histogram moves from mean ~48 -> ~28 that could explain kernel selection flip.

maya: replayed with real traffic window. batch histogram before vs after attached (short):
```
before: mean=51 median=48 p10=12 p90=96
after: mean=29 median=26 p10=6 p90=54
```

sam: that delta is big. Two quick experiments: (A) revert timer tweak in canary (B) disable kv-prefetch temporarily to see if evictions/prefetch contention is the amplifying factor. Which do we want first?

olivia: revert timer first — if that restores batch shapes and latency then we know timer is culprit. If revert helps but still slow, try (B).

maya: rolled back timer tweak on canary at 03:42, monitoring now. early signals: p95 trending back toward 430ms within 6m. throughput recovering.

rina: confirm — canary-group-7 p95 at 03:50 = 460ms, evictions/sec dropped to ~30.

leo: good. Still want to run controlled ablation: enable the timer tweak but bump token_budget_target up (e.g., from 64 -> 96) to see if larger budget prevents kernel fallback. Also run kernel-affinity experiment to prefer fast_kernel for smaller shapes if safe.

sam: note: kernel-affinity changes are risky because fast_kernel has edgecases for >max-seq; but we can do a gated experiment on canary only. I can run a small A/B where 10% of canary uses affinity override.

olivia: also need to re-evaluate KV prefetch heuristics. Current TTL/size tuned with old batch cadence. Prefetch which assumes sustained token cadence will thrash when pattern has many small bursts. We should record prefetch miss rates as a function of batch size and inter-arrival.

maya: action items:
- (maya) keep canary rolled back to baseline timer for next 24h, continue monitoring.
- (leo) run kernel-affinity experiment (canary A/B) + report p95/p99 and kernel_switch counts.
- (sam) prepare a kv-prefetch ablation toggle and a telemetry dashboard showing miss_rate vs batch_size.
- (olivia) simulate tuned token_budget_target (96) in replay and report shape + kernel_switch predictions.

olivia: small note — add a sampling hook to log kernel_choice per-batch in debug builds so we can correlate per-batch size -> kernel selection without full traces. cheap and useful.

rina: I'll keep an eye on incident noise and page if rollback doesn't hold.

maya: thanks, all. TL;DR: timer-skew tweak caused a subtle phase alignment -> batch sizes dropped -> kernel fallback + kv_prefetch thrash -> tail latency + throughput regression. Reverted in canary, metrics look better. We'll test token_budget and kernel-affinity as possible mitigations, and revisit prefetch config. :thumbsup:
